_comment: Domain knowledge that no general-purpose embedding model carries.
An advisor asking for 'address proof' wants the electricity bill, but nothing in the bill's
text is distributionally close to that phrase: it talks about meter readings and direct
debits. Five embedding models were measured on this corpus (all-MiniLM-L6-v2,
multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1, msmarco-MiniLM-L6-cos-v5, e5-small-v2, bge-small-en-v1.5) and all
five ranked the bill 13th or worse for that query while ranking every other probe first.
The association is procedural knowledge about which documents evidence what, so it is supplied
explicitly here rather than hoped for from the model.
A query reaches a rule by meaning, not by containing one of its phrases: each rule's paraphrases and
its concept name are embedded once at startup with the model the semantic arm searches with, and a
query fires the rule when its vector comes within search.concept-floor of one of them and within
search.concept-floor-ratio of the best rule's score — the second number is what stops 'proof of
address' dragging 'evidence of identity' in. So 'documents that show where the client lives' reaches
the address rule though none of its words appear here. Paraphrases are examples, not a list to
complete: state the requirement the way an advisor would, avoid words every client query carries
('client' on its own pulls unrelated queries towards a rule), add one when a real query shows up in
the search log with concepts=[] and should not have, then run ConceptFloorTest and read its table —
a phrasing close to another rule's wording narrows the margin between them.
Expansions widen the semantic arm only. The lexical arm exists to match exact tokens, and OR-ing
extra terms into it would cost precision for recall the semantic arm already provides; the sparse arm
was measured with the probes and without and they changed no rank, only page length.

paraphrases: something that shows where the client lives
something that confirms the client's home address
a way to prove who someone is
how a person proves their identity
confirming that a person is who they say they are
proof of what the client earns

rules.concept: acting for someone who has lost capacity
paraphrases: who can act for someone who can no longer manage their own affairs
someone appointed to make decisions for a person who has lost capacity
expansions: lasting power of attorney attorney appointed

paraphrases: what the life policy pays out on death
